identity.fantasy: A battle bard and field commander who turns ballads, Tempo, formations, banners, drums, and timed marches into raid-wide momentum.
identity.one_line: A bard-commander using Tempo, songs, banners, drums, and party auras. It contributes damage while maintaining Battle Bard effects and choosing the right manuscript, march, or banner for the encounter. Its strength is group amplification, but personal rotation and raid-buff timing compete for attention.

mechanics.core_loop: Open in Line Formation for Harrowing Melody and Advance, deploy the chosen standard and Battle Drums, shift into Assault Formation, stack major buffs, then prioritize Dragonslayer or Conqueror, Empowered Ram at the intended Tempo state, Reprisal procs, and Glorious Arena while protecting Energy for the next formation transition.

modes.name: Inspiring Leader
modes.structural_description: You pledge to inspire your allies in the midst of battle, transforming your Pulverize and your Broad Sweep into Ballads.

modes.name: Tempo
modes.structural_description: Level 10 PassiveCasting Ballads now grants Tempo, stacking 3 times. Upon reaching 3 stacks of Tempo, you consume them to perform a Sound of War, striking all enemies within 8 yds for 71 + 12.74% AP Magic damage.Tempo (Proc)Critical strike chance increased by 2%, stacking 3 times.

modes.name: Banner Boy
modes.structural_description: Increases your haste by 5% and the movement speed granted by Line Formation by 8%.

modes.name: Dissonance
modes.structural_description: Damage dealt by Sound of War now has a 25% chance to reduce enemies' resistances by 75 and increases their Magic damage taken by -2% for 8 seconds.

modes.name: Battle Drums
modes.structural_description: Place down 3 Battle Drums around you for 1 minute. Allies may click on the drums to increase their critical strike chance, haste, damage, and healing done by 10% and causes their damage dealt to trigger a Sound of War for their next 5 instances of damage or 30 seconds.

modes.structural_description: Adds 5% to the value of Echoes of War.In addition, performing a Sound of War now has a 40% chance to echo, striking an additional time after 0.5 sec. Can only occur once per sec.

modes.name: Field Commander

mechanics.single_target: Personal damage comes from a priority system driven by buffs, Tempo, Empowered Ram, Reprisal, and arena effects rather than a fixed repeating rotation.
mechanics.aoe: Sound of War, Dragonslayer, banners, drums, and party-triggered Echoes of War create strong pack and group amplification.
mechanics.movement_and_target_switching: Advance, formations, Charge, marches, and high mobility help reposition, but the opener asks the player to place drums and swap stances quickly.
mechanics.defense_and_control: Guardian defensive tools, AoE control, crowd-control immunity, and group protections make the support unusually durable.
mechanics.group_utility: Its defining value is a large raid-buff inventory, with different physical, magical, dungeon, and raid packages that must be coordinated with other supports.

failure_modes.text: Poor formation timing can strand the player at low Energy, while overlapping another support's raid buffs or placing clickable drums badly wastes much of the spec's unique value.

Movement or a target swap can interrupt the intended payoff: advance, formations, charge, marches, and high mobility help reposition, but the opener asks the player to place drums and swap stances quickly.

Spending recovery or control too early leaves less protection for the next pressure event: guardian defensive tools, aoe control, crowd-control immunity, and group protections make the support unusually durable.

enjoy_if.text: You want a genuinely supportive battle bard with a demanding melee priority system and responsibility for the whole group's buff plan.

You enjoy the spec's core cadence: open in line formation for harrowing melody and advance, deploy the chosen standard and battle drums, shift into assault formation, stack major buffs, then prioritize dragonslayer or conqueror, empowered ram at the intended tempo state, reprisal procs, and glorious arena while protecting energy for the next formation transition.

avoid_if.text: You dislike stance swapping, proc variance, raid coordination, or doing work whose payoff appears on teammates' meters.
You dislike the positioning or swap constraint that advance, formations, charge, marches, and high mobility help reposition, but the opener asks the player to place drums and swap stances quickly.

praise.theme: The current guide praises its raid-wide buff range, useful damage, survivability, mobility, AoE control, and crowd-control immunity.

frustrations.theme: The same guide calls it overly complex, RNG dependent, prone to zero-Energy downtime, and potentially off-putting because of stance swaps.

contested.theme: Its reported personal DPS understates a role explicitly designed to move meaningful damage into allied buffs and Echoes of War.

gaps: Four reported viable builds are not separately profiled.
Raid contribution lacks a controlled group-level comparison.

claims.text: The August Build Hub guide describes Inspiration as an unusually complex stance-swapping support with broad raid buffs, strong survivability and mobility, AoE control, and good damage, but also RNG damage and possible zero-Energy downtime. It documents a Line-to-Assault opener, Tempo and Empowered Ram timing, Reprisal priority, fast-weapon preference, different dungeon and raid buff packages, and a requirement to coordinate non-overlapping talents with other supports.
claims.notes: The author reports four viable builds and documents one personal-DPS-oriented version.

claims.text: The July compilation reports Inspiration at 2,562 in a support or off-role context, and the August Mythic inventory lists 44 records. The current guide states that Echoes of War can transfer substantial damage into party members, so personal DPS alone is incomplete.
claims.notes: No normalized group-contribution metric is available.

claims.text: Inspiration has both rotational and social setup burden because its raid value depends on choosing the right shared buffs, avoiding overlap with other supports, and placing interactive effects where allies can use them.
claims.notes: This burden is part of the intended support identity, not merely button count.
